content.text: {"primary_meaning":"A “sign” is most commonly understood functionally as a visible event, act, object, or miracle that points beyond itself to divine activity and confirms God’s message, promise, presence, or the authority of God’s messenger. It does not have one fixed symbolic referent across Scripture.","primary_basis":["Exodus 4:1–9, 29–31 — miraculous signs authenticate Moses’ divine commission.","Exodus 7:3; Deuteronomy 4:34 — signs and wonders reveal God’s power in the exodus.","Isaiah 7:14 — a divinely given sign confirms a prophetic promise.","John 2:11 — Jesus’ sign reveals his glory and leads disciples to believe.","John 20:30–31 — Jesus’ signs are recorded to support faith in his identity.","Acts 2:22; Hebrews 2:3–4 — signs authenticate Jesus and the apostolic proclamation.","Romans 4:11 — circumcision is called a sign and seal of covenantal righteousness."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"A miraculous work or “wonder,” emphasizing supernatural power rather than a symbolic object or encoded meaning.","basis":["Exodus 7:3","Acts 2:22","Acts 4:30","2 Corinthians 12:12"],"prominence":"dominant"},{"meaning":"A covenant marker that identifies a people, recalls a promise, or signifies an enduring relationship with God.","basis":["Genesis 9:12–17 — the rainbow as covenant sign.","Genesis 17:11 — circumcision as covenant sign.","Exodus 31:13, 16–17 — the Sabbath as a sign between God and Israel.","Romans 4:11 — circumcision as sign and seal."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"A prophetic symbol or omen, including an enacted sign, that depicts or anticipates a coming judgment, deliverance, or historical event.","basis":["Isaiah 8:18","Isaiah 20:3","Ezekiel 4:1–3","Ezekiel 12:6, 11"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"An eschatological indicator marking the approach of divine judgment, Christ’s return, or the consummation of history.","basis":["Matthew 24:3, 24, 30","Luke 21:7, 11, 25","Revelation 12:1, 3","Revelation 15:1"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"In sacramental theology, a material element or rite that signifies—and in many traditions also conveys or participates in—divine grace.","basis":["Romans 4:11","Matthew 26:26–28","1 Corinthians 10:16","1 Peter 3:21"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"A specific reference to Jesus’ death, burial, and resurrection through the “sign of Jonah,” rather than a general meaning of the word sign.","basis":["Matthew 12:38–40","Matthew 16:1–4","Luke 11:29–30"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"A deceptive or counterfeit supernatural manifestation that supports false teaching or rebellion; a sign therefore does not automatically prove divine approval.","basis":["Deuteronomy 13:1–3","Matthew 24:24","2 Thessalonians 2:9–10","Revelation 13:13–14"],"prominence":"common"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is broad consensus about the term’s general function—something perceptible that points beyond itself or authenticates a claim—but no settled, single symbolic meaning. Its referent depends on context: miracle, covenant marker, prophetic token, eschatological omen, sacramental element, or deceptive wonder."}
